result: h07. **Where the URL comes from (why the browser requests it at all):** `convertUserFromStore` rewrites a base64 avatar into the path `/file/users/{username}/avatar` — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:31-40` — which the React `` renders — `web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:13-14`. **The serving path for `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`:** ``` fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124 (registered from server/server.go:81-82) FileServerService.serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 FileServerService.getCurrentUser → auth.Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708-712 (only when s.Profile.AllowAnonymous() is false) FileServerService.getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715-717 store.Store.GetUser — store/user.go:148 (userCache checked only when find.ID is set; a username lookup always falls through) store.Store.ListUsers — store/user.go:136 Driver.ListUsers — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (also store/db/postgres/user.go:87, store/db/mysql/user.go:84) SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ? — store/db/sqlite/user.go:151-165, scanned into store.User.AvatarURL at :189 ``` Back up the stack, `serveUserAvatar` decodes `user.AvatarURL` — the avatar is stored as a base64 data URI in the `user.avatar_url` column, not as a file or attachment — via `FileServerService.parseDataURI` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737`), rejects any MIME type outside `avatarAllowedTypes` (`:75-83`), sets nosniff/DENY/CSP headers plus `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`, and writes the bytes with `c.Blob` (`:196-209`). Two things worth noting: - The data layer is the `user` table itself — there is no filesystem or S3 hop for avatars, unlike attachments (`serveAttachmentFile`, same file:132). - `/memos.api.v1.UserService/GetUserAvatar` appears in the ACL allowlist (`server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go:25`) but has no implementation anywhere in `server/` or the web client; the fileserver route above is the only live path.
